title: At the hotel
summary: Check in at a hotel, ask about breakfast and the lift, and make polite requests with لَوْ سَمَحْتَ, هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ…؟ and أَرْجُو أَنْ…
intro: In the evening Yusuf drives Daniel and Layla to their hotel near the centre of Amman. At the reception desk you ask for things, and Arabic has several ways to make a request polite: add لَوْ سَمَحْتَ (if you allow, excuse me) or مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (please), ask هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ…؟ (can you…?), or begin with أَرْجُو أَنْ… (I would ask you to…). After أَنْ the verb ends in -a, as always.
objectives: Check in at a hotel with a booking in your name
Make polite requests with لَوْ سَمَحْتَ, هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ…؟ and أَرْجُو أَنْ…
Ask when breakfast starts and where the lift is
Use the words hotel, reception, night, booking, lift and password

realLife.title: A small hotel with a view
realLife.story: Yusuf has found his friends a small family hotel on one of Amman's hills. The receptionist is friendly, both rooms have a balcony with a view of the old Citadel, and the internet password is written on a little card at the desk.

sentences.en: Excuse me, where is the lift?
sentences.literal: if you allow, where (is) the lift?

mistakes.wrong: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، أَيْنَ الْمِصْعَد؟ (to a woman)
mistakes.why: To a woman say law samaḥti, with -ti at the end.

sentences.ar: هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تُوقِظَنَا فِي السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة؟
sentences.en: Could you wake us at seven o'clock?
sentences.literal: are you able that you wake us at the seventh hour?

mistakes.why: After an the verb ends in -a, even before an ending like -nā: tūqiẓanā.

sentences.en: We have a booking for two nights.
sentences.literal: at us (is) a booking for two nights

mistakes.why: After a preposition like li the dual ends in -ayni, not -āni.

sentences.en: The hotel is small, but it is clean and comfortable.
sentences.literal: the hotel (is) small, but it (is) clean and comfortable

sentences.en: Please order a taxi for us.
sentences.literal: I hope that you order for us a taxi

sentences.en: The keys are with the receptionist.
sentences.literal: the keys (are) at (the) employee (of) the reception

dialogue.title: Checking in
dialogue.culture: Hotels in Jordan ask for every guest's passport at check-in, and breakfast is usually included: bread, cheese, olives, hummus and sweet tea. At the end of the evening people say تُصْبِحُونَ عَلَى خَيْر, literally 'may you wake up to something good': good night.

lines.ar: وَصَلْنَا! هٰذَا هُوَ الْفُنْدُق. هُوَ صَغِير، لٰكِنَّهُ نَظِيف وَمُرِيح، وَقَرِيب مِنْ وَسَطِ الْبَلَد.
lines.en: Here we are! This is the hotel. It's small, but it's clean and comfortable, and it's close to the city centre.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر، أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا فِي عَمَّان! كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكُمْ؟
lines.en: Good evening, and welcome to Amman! How can I help you?

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. عِنْدَنَا حَجْز بِاسْمِي، لَيْلَى: غُرْفَتَانِ لِلَيْلَتَيْنِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Good evening. We have a booking in my name, Layla: two rooms for two nights, please.

lines.ar: لَحْظَة، لَوْ سَمَحْتِ… نَعَم، غُرْفَتَانِ لِلَيْلَتَيْنِ. جَوَازُ السَّفَر، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، وَجَوَازُكَ أَيْضًا يَا أُسْتَاذ.
lines.en: One moment, please… yes, two rooms for two nights. Your passport, please, and yours too, sir.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلْ. وَلَوْ سَمَحْتَ، هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تُعْطِيَنَا غُرْفَتَيْنِ فِي الطَّابِق الْأَخِير؟ نُحِبُّ أَنْ نَرَى الْمَنْظَر.
lines.en: Here you are. And if you don't mind, could you give us two rooms on the top floor? We'd love to see the view.

lines.ar: طَبْعًا. الْغُرْفَتَانِ فِي الطَّابِق الْخَامِس، وَمِنَ الشُّرْفَة تَرَوْنَ جَبَلَ الْقَلْعَة. تَفَضَّلُوا الْمَفَاتِيح.
lines.en: Of course. Both rooms are on the fifth floor, and from the balcony you can see the Citadel hill. Here are your keys.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! وَالْفُطُور؟ فِي أَيِّ سَاعَة يَبْدَأُ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، وَأَيْنَ الْمَطْعَم؟
lines.en: Thank you very much! And breakfast? What time does it start, please, and where is the restaurant?

lines.ar: الْفُطُور مِنَ السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة إِلَى السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة فِي الْمَطْعَم، فِي الطَّابِق الْأَوَّل. وَالْمِصْعَد هُنَاكَ، عَلَى الْيَمِين.
lines.en: Breakfast is from seven to ten o'clock in the restaurant on the first floor. And the lift is over there, on the right.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز. وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تُوقِظَنَا فِي السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة غَدًا، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ. نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَخْرُجَ مُبَكِّرًا.
lines.en: Excellent. And I'd ask you to wake us at seven tomorrow, please. We want to go out early.

lines.ar: بِكُلِّ سُرُور. أَتَّصِلُ بِكُمَا فِي السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة. هَلْ تَحْتَاجَانِ إِلَى شَيْء آخَر؟
lines.en: With pleasure. I'll call you both at seven. Do you need anything else?

lines.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ: مَا كَلِمَةُ السِّرّ لِلْإِنْتَرْنِت؟ وَهَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَطْلُبَ لَنَا تَاكْسِي غَدًا؟
lines.en: Yes, please: what's the password for the internet? And could you order us a taxi tomorrow?

lines.ar: لَا، لَا تَطْلُبْ تَاكْسِي يَا أَخِي! أَنَا آتِي بِسَيَّارَتِي فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة، وَنَذْهَبُ مَعًا إِلَى وَسَطِ الْبَلَد.
lines.en: No, no, don't order a taxi, my friend! I'll come with my car at eight, and we'll go to the city centre together.

lines.ar: كَمَا تُرِيدُونَ. كَلِمَةُ السِّرّ عَلَى هٰذِهِ الْبِطَاقَة. نَتَمَنَّى لَكُمْ إِقَامَة سَعِيدَة فِي عَمَّان!
lines.en: As you wish. The password is on this card. We wish you a pleasant stay in Amman!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا يُوسُف، أَنْتَ صَدِيق رَائِع. وَالْآنَ أَرْجُو أَنْ تَسْمَحَ لَنَا بِالنَّوْم، فَالْيَوْمُ كَانَ طَوِيلًا!
lines.en: Thank you, Yusuf, you're a wonderful friend. And now please let us go to sleep, because it's been a long day!

lines.ar: طَبْعًا! تُصْبِحُونَ عَلَى خَيْر، وَأَرَاكُمْ غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة أَمَامَ الْفُنْدُق.
lines.en: Of course! Good night, and see you tomorrow at eight o'clock in front of the hotel.
segs: and I see you (to several people)

reading.title: A night in Amman
reading.ar: وَصَلَ دَانْيَال وَلَيْلَى إِلَى الْفُنْدُق فِي الْمَسَاء مَعَ يُوسُف. الْفُنْدُق صَغِير وَنَظِيف، وَهُوَ قَرِيب مِنْ وَسَطِ الْبَلَد. الْغُرْفَتَانِ فِي الطَّابِق الْخَامِس، وَمِنَ الشُّرْفَة يَرَى دَانْيَال جَبَلَ الْقَلْعَة. يَبْدَأُ الْفُطُور فِي السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة، وَفِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة يَأْتِي يُوسُف بِسَيَّارَتِهِ.
reading.en: Daniel and Layla arrived at the hotel in the evening with Yusuf. The hotel is small and clean, and it is close to the city centre. The two rooms are on the fifth floor, and from the balcony Daniel can see the Citadel hill. Breakfast starts at seven o'clock, and at eight Yusuf comes with his car.

quiz.prompt: How many nights is the booking for?
On which floor are the rooms?
Why doesn't Yusuf want the receptionist to order a taxi?
options: he is coming with his own car

quiz.prompt: Which word ends in tāʾ marbūṭa (ة)?

completion: Well done! You can check in at a hotel, ask for what you need and make any request polite. Next time: booking a room by phone.
